---
title: "Russian economy on life support"
description: "As Western firms withdrew, Chinese exports to Russia more than doubled, giving Beijing outsized leverage over Moscow's wartime economy."
date: "2024-03-27"
categories: [ukraine, russia-economy]
---

Sanctions after the 2022 invasion pushed Russia into deep economic dependence
on China: Chinese exports to Russia jumped from an average $52 billion over
2017–2021 to $111 billion in 2023, as European and American exports
collapsed. That concentration cuts against Russia — the piece argues China is
positioned to charge above-market prices for what it sells while buying
Russian energy at a discount, turning a wartime lifeline into significant
economic leverage over Moscow.

**Originally published on Substack**, March 27, 2024.
